newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi River could re-open Wednesday - C.Guard.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi River could re-open Wednesday - C.Guard.

text.p: The Mississippi River could re-open Wednesday after a barge leaking petrochemicals is cleared away, the Coast Guard said.
The river was closed late Monday after a tow of 25 barges hit a bridge in north Baton Rouge, La., turning upside down a barge carrying an 10,000 barrels of a product used to make gasoline.

"A barge carrying a crane is coming at 1000 (CST/1100 EST) to turn the barge right-side up, and that can take several hours," said Commander Kenneth Parris of the Coast Guard Marine Safety Office, New Orleans Operations Center.
Asked if the river could re-open Wednesday, Parris replied, "It's certainly possible."
The barge is believed to be leaking the petrochemical through vents.
But Parris said the petrochemical, pyrolysis gasoline is easily diluted by the flow of the river. It evaporates quickly, he added.

Flooding north of Louisiana and heavy rains created high water and a swift current on the river. Ironically, the string of barges had been carrying extra manpower to take precautionary measures at the time of the mishap.

"This was the third collision with the bridge a tow has has had in three days," said Parris, noting the latest tow to collide was carrying lighter than usual cargo due to the tougher river conditions.
Parris said it is unknown how much of the petrochemical had leaked.
